title: [finding] a gantt view's authored view-level `navigation` reaches nothing — `ListView` forwards it neither as a prop nor on the view schema, so `ObjectGantt` always falls back to its own `mode: 'drawer'` default
body:
Measured statically while implementing objectui#7222. Filed unassigned. This sharpens objectui#7222's "Consequence 3 — SUSPECTED, not measured", which asked whether a gantt's authored navigation is honoured; it is **not browser-verified** here either, but the two code paths that would have to carry it are both measurably empty.

## Measured — three reads, `origin/main` at 1e7fe0a65

1. **`ObjectGantt` owns a record drawer of its own.** `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` imports `RecordDetailDrawer` from `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and computes `const navConfig = schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' };`. So a task click opens something regardless of any host callback — which is why objectui#7222 was right not to treat the dropped `onRowClick` as a defect on its own.

2. **The host callback never arrives.** `ListView`'s `baseProps` carries `onRowClick: navigation.handleClick`, and `ObjectGanttRenderer` destructures `({ schema })` only, so it is dropped one layer up (objectui#7222; pinned in `plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.hostDataProp-7210.test.tsx`).

3. **The authored config never arrives either — this is the new part.** `ObjectGantt` reads `schema.navigation`, so the schema route would still work even with every prop dropped. It is empty: `baseProps` in `ListView.tsx` declares no `navigation` key (`objectName`, `fields`, `filter`, `sort`, `className`, `showSearch`, `onRowClick`, `rowHeight`, `hideRowHeightToggle`, plus the column-state callback), and the `case 'gantt'` branch of `viewComponentSchema` adds only `data`, `startDateField`, `endDateField`, `progressField`, `dependenciesField`, `titleField` and the two gantt config bags. `schema.navigation` is consumed by `ListView` itself (`useNavigationOverlay`) and forwarded no further.

Net: a list view authored `navigation: { mode: 'page' }` (or `modal`, or `split`) renders a gantt that opens a drawer. The other view types do not have this problem for the opposite reason — they consume `onRowClick`, so the host's overlay decides.

## What is NOT claimed

Not driven in a browser. Nothing here says which layer should own the fix: forwarding `navigation` on the gantt view schema and forwarding host props to the chart are two different repairs, and the second is entangled with the open ceiling decision on objectui#7210 half 2. Recording the measurement so the next person does not have to re-derive it.

Refs: objectui#7222 (Consequence 3, where this was flagged as unverified), objectui#7210.
